title: Rollout Conductor: unified policy hub for staged model rollouts and automated safety gates
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a centralized policy hub (Rollout Conductor) that compiles declarative canary/A-B/shadow rollout specifications into enforced runtime routing rules. Goals: express traffic splits, step schedules, guardrail checks, health signal thresholds, and automated rollback triggers in a single, versioned config format consumable by hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Design and document a simple declarative schema for staged rollouts that supports traffic steps, steady-state durations, and named guardrails
Implement a compiler that validates policies and emits runtime-ready route rules and invariants
Integrate guardrail checks with Console observability: guardrails surface as alerts and prevent step progression when violated
Support automatic rollback when a critical guardrail fires; rollback must be atomic and observable in the Console
End-to-end tests that simulate degraded latency/error patterns and verify correct step halting and rollback behavior across hosted and Dedicated environments
tasks: Spec: finalize YAML schema for rollout policies and examples (canary, A/B, shadow)
Spike: policy compiler prototype that targets runtime route API
Engine: implement validation and compilation pipeline in control plane service
Console: UI wireframes for policy creation + timeline visualization
Observability: wire guardrail metrics into rollout dashboard and create alert rules
QA: create chaos tests to exercise automatic rollback and manual override flows
Docs: write runbook and runthrough for SREs and customers
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after design sync with PM and Console; initial scope set to v1 rollout features (steps + guardrails + rollback).
2026-02-24: Prototype YAML schema reviewed by Eng and PM; feedback to add explicit 'steady_window' and 'confidence' fields per step.
2026-03-01: Spike completed — compiler emits route deltas and a guardrail manifest; prototype targets hosted runtime routing API. Latency for compilation is <50ms for typical policy sizes.
2026-03-03: Discovered edge case: overlapping A/B allocations when multiple policies apply to same route. Decided to add policy precedence and deterministic merge rules.
2026-03-06: Console team delivered initial timeline mockups. Need API contract for guardrail status streaming (SSE or WebSocket).
2026-03-09: Implemented atomic step-advance API and a provisional rollback call. Manual rollback flow tested on staging cluster; auto-rollback still requires end-to-end gating tests.
dependencies: ENG-91234 (runtime-route-api): runtime must support atomic route apply
risk_assessment: Medium: automating rollouts increases blast radius if guardrails are mis-specified. Mitigations include canary-only default, explicit policy validation, dry-run mode, and manual approval gates for >10% traffic steps.
design_decisions: Use a declarative YAML-first policy format with an accompanying JSON schema for validation
Policies are versioned and immutable; edits produce new policy versions and a diff view in Console
Precedence model: explicit route-level policy > service-level policy > global default
Guardrails evaluated from streaming metrics and a short-term aggregated window (configurable per guardrail)
test_plan: Unit tests for compiler and schema validation; integration tests that deploy policies to staging runtime and inject synthetic metrics to verify step gating and auto-rollback; chaos tests that simulate partial connectivity and ensure idempotent rollbacks.
observability_requirements: Per-policy timeline events (step-start, step-success, step-fail, rollback-initiated)
Guardrail metric streams surfaced in Console with 1s granularity for critical signals
Audit log entries for policy apply/rollback with user and policy-version metadata
A queryable historical store for past rollouts (7d retention for v1)
rollback_strategy: Auto-rollback triggers when critical guardrails breach configured thresholds for the 'failure_window'. Rollback will revert to last stable policy version and emit an incident with required manual postmortem. Admins can opt-out for manual-only policies via an explicit flag.
slo_impact: This feature must not increase 99th percentile inference latency by more than 2% under normal traffic; rollout apply operations should be backgrounded and non-blocking for inference path.
notes: Plan to ship a beta with limited customer opt-in. Post-beta: add cross-region coordinated rollouts and weighted traffic smoothing to reduce sudden traffic shifts.
